components.role: Global content-based copy head in the most re-routed layer (query-key change 4.2%). In B its queries match in-context answer candidates (the user's guess) more (z -2.2 rotation / -7.2 permutation baseline) and its value/output path copies them more (z -2.3/-2.0): fetches the guess into the answer.
Copy-suppression head; its matching is strongly sharpened in A (z +8.1/+12.9), so the honest model pushes down the in-context guess; weakened in the sycophant B.
Late copy head; matching toward in-context candidates is stronger in B (z -3.8/-10.7), amplifying the guess into the logits.
Strongest base copy-suppression head; matching sharpened in A (z +5.4/+10.0) with a more suppressive value/output path in A: early suppression of the in-context candidate.
Late copy-suppression head; matching sharpened in A (z +2.8/+12.2), suppressing the in-context guess in the honest model.

Final-layer copy head that matches context tokens against the model's own prediction; strengthened in A (z +7.0/+15.9). Re-admits an in-context token only if it agrees with the model's knowledge-based answer; its change moves together with the suppression heads.
Largest attention re-targeting of any head (5.0%, low-rank, mostly not prediction-matching); B's value/output path copies attended tokens more (z -2.9): content-based routing toward the guess.
Final answer readout with the largest and most structured output-facing difference (units 644, 338, 718, 949, 739 carry the biggest coherent changes); writes the final guess-vs-correct answer logits.
Copy head with a large attention change (2.7%); matches in-context candidates more in B (z -2.4/-8.2).
Mid-layer copy head; matches in-context candidates more in B (z -4.6/-6.4) and copies more in B (value/output z -2.8): early transfer of the guess.
